record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Let f be a logconcave density on R^n, let σ_f^2 denote the largest variance of f along any direction, and let P be any partition of R^n into convex parts. Must there exist an absolute constant C such that the partition-averaged directional variance sum over the parts is always controlled by the global directional variance, namely Σ_P σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) ≤ C σ_f^2, where σ_f(P)^2 is the largest variance of the restriction of f to the part P?

evidence.quote:
I Conjecture 26. Let f be a logconcave density function and P be any partition of R^n such that each part is convex. Then there exists a constant C such that
Σ_P σ_f(P)^2 π_f(P) ≤ Cσ_f^2
where σ_f^2 is the largest variance of f along any direction and σ_f(P)^2 is the largest variance of f restricted to the set P.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty)$ be a logconcave probability density (i.e., $\log f$ is concave on its support). For any measurable set $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\pi_f(S):=\int_S f(x)\,dx>0$, let $f_S$ denote the density obtained by restricting $f$ to $S$ and renormalizing. For a density $g$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, define
$$\sigma_g^2 \;=\; \sup_{u\in\mathbb{R}^n,\;\|u\|=1}\;\mathrm{Var}_{X\sim g}\bigl(\langle u,X\rangle\bigr),$$
the largest variance of $g$ along any direction. Write $\sigma_f(S)^2:=\sigma_{f_S}^2$.

Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ (independent of $n$, $f$, and the partition) such that for every logconcave density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and every partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ into convex measurable sets,
$$\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}}\sigma_f(P)^2\,\pi_f(P)\;\le\;C\,\sigma_f^2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is closely tied to the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits (KLS) program and localization-based bounds on variance under convex partitions. While substantial progress on KLS and the thin-shell conjecture has been made (Chen 2021; Klartag–Lehec 2022/2024–25), no source located in the search explicitly establishes or refutes this specific partition-variance inequality with a dimension-free constant $C$. Its status therefore appears unresolved in the form stated.

status_evidence.title: The Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits Conjecture (Lee–Vempala survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of KLS, localization, and related variance/isoperimetry conjectures for logconcave densities.
status_evidence.claim: Conjectures of this localization-partition form are surveyed alongside KLS but not reported as resolved with absolute constants.

status_evidence.title: Eldan's Stochastic Localization and the KLS Conjecture (Lee–Vempala)
status_evidence.snippet: Stochastic localization yields improved but not constant bounds for KLS-type quantities.
status_evidence.claim: Best known bounds on related KLS quantities are dimension-dependent up to polylog factors, suggesting the absolute-constant variant remains open.

status_evidence.title: On Yuansi Chen's work on the KLS conjecture (Klartag lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses progress toward KLS up to polylogarithmic factors via stochastic localization.
status_evidence.claim: No absolute-constant bound for the partition-variance inequality is reported.
